evidence.title: Read independently authorized Command Tasks linked to a selected Incident Detail
evidence.goal: Complete the canonical Incident coordination read flow: display existing Command Task ownership/status/timestamp next to the selected Incident, using an independently authorized Incident->Task relation and the exact existing Command Owner.List/CanRead Task projection. No Task creation, assignment, mutation or duplicate authorization engine.
outputs: Existing GET /command/incident-detail shows only independently read-authorized linked Task id, owner/status and source updatedAt, without new endpoint or mutation.
Local loopback with analyst sees synthetic linked Task; commander has Incident permission but no Task.read and sees no Task ID.
Direct Go unit tests and real Go HTTP fixture verify positive, negative, malformed, lost permission, legacy behavior, oversized owner and cancelled request.
acceptance_tests: Authorized Incident with scoped Task relation, Task in existing Command owner listing and individual Task CanRead=true => Task visibly listed in existing Incident Detail.
Incident reader lacking Task.read sees neither linked Task ID nor source metadata, including on later reaccess.
Broken tenant/env/incident/duplicate relation, malformed Task owner data, cancelled request, failed sources and bound overflows fail closed without partial HTML.
Legacy owner implementation without Task relation interface still shows Incident Detail and explicitly partial Task source.
Existing three GitHub workflows on exact SHA all pass, including workqueue Go race/vet, local real HTTP tests and mandatory engineering security checks.

rules: Strict tenant isolation and permission checking
